note.backdrop: The sell-off hit its low in the late morning and partly recovered. At 11:02 a.m. ET the Nasdaq 100 fund was -4.38% and SPY -2.76% (StockTitan); at this check (12:35 p.m. ET) SPY is -1.6%, QQQ -2.8%, small caps -0.4%, and the VIX +24.2%. Three pieces of news landed at 8:30 a.m. ET and after: third-quarter growth was revised up to a 4.3% annual rate from 3.4%; the PCE price index was 3.8% higher than a year earlier (3.3% without food and energy); and the US Trade Representative proposed tariffs of up to 35% on goods from 14 economies (proposals, comments due Jan 5, 2027). Yet the 10-year yield fell 0.07 pt, almost twice its usual day, and homebuilders rose: money went to safety despite the hot inflation number (inferred from the drivers).

read.says: Nov 25 by 11:03 a.m. ET: QQQ -4.38% and SPY -2.76% against Tuesday's close (about 96% of Monday's QQQ gain gone); AMD -8.99%, 11.4% below Friday's close; AMD, Broadcom and Micron have lost all of Monday's jump; Lam Research -11.64%; Ambarella -18.98%; HP +10.38% (Q4 revenue $16.0 billion, +9.3%); BEA: Q3 GDP revised to 4.3% from 3.4%, October PCE prices +3.8% from a year earlier, 3.3% without food and energy; jobless claims 189,000; new home sales 701,000 annual rate; USTR proposed tariffs up to 35% (Vietnam) and 15% (EU, Japan) on 14 economies, comments due Jan 5, 2027; Deere turned higher after the open; Pharming -16.79% after pausing RUCONEST production.

themes.beneath: Nvidia -7.6%, -4.6% of its own beyond the market. The whole of Monday's rally rested on one board decision; two and a half sessions later the group is back where it started, and the memory squeeze named by Ambarella, HPE and Dell's preview (memory and component costs) is the reason given for the doubt (s17, s18). An economist on CNBC said he is buying the dip 'very slowly' (s30, opinion).
themes.cause: The chip sell-off deepened after the open on AI spending fears (s15, s31, s33, s37): AMD, Broadcom and Micron have lost all of Monday's jump, and the Nasdaq 100 fund gave back about 96% of its +7.00% Monday by 11:02 a.m. ET (StockTitan).
themes.mechanism: Semiconductors' median -4.1%; the chip-equipment makers fall with them (Lam Research -10.2%, most of it the market at its beta of 3.24), and so do the AI power and construction builders: Quanta -6.7%, Jacobs -5.5%, both with no company news (s23, s37).
themes.name: AI hardware gives back all of Monday
themes.watch: The close: whether chips end at the lows or recover with the market, as they did late morning.

themes.beneath: In a market falling on fear (VIX +24.2%), safety demand for Treasuries outweighed the inflation print (inferred). The tariffs are proposals with comments due January 5, so their effect on any stock is not visible yet.
themes.cause: BEA revised third-quarter growth to 4.3% and put October PCE inflation at 3.8% (core 3.3%); jobless claims fell to 189,000; USTR proposed new tariffs on 14 economies.
themes.mechanism: Hot inflation would usually lift yields and press on rate-sensitive stocks; instead the 10-year yield fell 0.07 pt and the stocks most tied to it rose (Toll Brothers +2.9%, D.R. Horton +2.6%, Rocket +4.5%).
themes.name: Hot inflation, faster growth, new tariffs, and yields down
themes.watch: Whether yields stay lower into the close and Friday's half day.
